notes: Live Shopify storefront, direct HTTP fetch worked throughout, no blocking. Enumerated all 155 collections via /en-intl/collections.json for new-arrival-type titles/handles (new-in, new arrival, just in, latest, recently added, etc.) - no dedicated New Arrivals collection exists. The mega-menu on every shop section (Wallpaper, Fabric, Home Decor, Furniture) does show a link labelled 'New In', but inspection of its href (e.g. /en-intl/collections/wallpaper#/sort:published_at:desc) shows it is NOT a distinct listing - it is the section's own existing category collection (Wallpaper/Fabric/Home Decor/Furniture, already covered by the separate Home Decor/Furniture category projects) re-sorted client-side by publish date via a URL fragment, same product set and same underlying collection page/count as the parent category. This is an arbitrary date-sort filter on an existing category, not a genuine standalone New Arrivals PLP with its own product set or count, so it was excluded per the brief's 'arbitrary date-filter pages' exclusion rather than recorded as a row. Also found one collection, handle 'trade-exclusive-preview' / title 'New Season Preview Trade' (80 products per collections.json), present in collections.json but not linked anywhere in the site's main navigation, header, or footer for retail customers - it is explicitly a trade/wholesale-only preview of an upcoming season's range (title and page copy both say 'Trade'), not a public 'recently added to catalogue' merchandising concept aimed at regular shoppers. Excluded as out-of-scope (B2B preview page, not a retail New Arrivals PLP) rather than flagged ambiguous, since both the trade-only framing and the absence from customer-facing nav are clear signals, not a coin-flip. Site's own search (/en-intl/search?q=new+arrivals&type=product) returned a static 'No results' string for this and every other query tried (including terms with confirmed real listings), so it is not usable as a discriminating signal here; navigation + full collections.json enumeration was used instead per the zero-result-is-not-proof-of-absence rule. Conclusion: no genuine New Arrivals PLP exists on this storefront.
